articles.title: League One clubs aim for further curbs on spending as budgets continue to spiral
articles.summary: Wage bills in third tier have increased by 15% this season. ‘Luxury tax’ and three-year limits on losses considered. League One clubs want to introduce new spending restrictions to reduce losses by limiting investment from owners.
body: Clubs in the division voted to tighten the rules last summer by reducing spending limits from 60% to 50% of turnover, and removed a staggered approach to owner investment, so that only 50% of equity injections can be spent on squad costs, with the rest assigned to infrastructure projects. Less than six months later many want to go further.

The Guardian has learned that two proposed models are being considered: a cap on the amount clubs can lose over three years, and the introduction of a luxury tax by which 50% of owner investment above a capped threshold would be redistributed to their rivals – with the former proposal seen as the favoured outcome.

The move to introduce more spending curbs comes despite a legal challenge to the existing rules from the Professional Footballers’ Association, which launched proceedings in August on the grounds that the clubs had failed to abide by the terms of their membership of the professional negotiating and consultative committee.
An attempt by League One and League Two to introduce salary caps of £2.5m and £1.5m respectively was withdrawn in 2021 after the PFA took them to an independent arbitration panel.

articles.title: Bethell faces fitness race for South Africa Tests after being ruled out of Australia tour
articles.summary: All-rounder sent back to UK with swelling on knee. South Africa Test series begins on 17 December. Jacob Bethell is battling to be fit for England’s Test series in South Africa next month after being ruled out of the white-ball tour of Australia.
body: The 23-year-old underwent surgery on his right knee at the end of August and while he was not expected to be ready for the one-day internationals that start in Perth on Friday, it was hoped he would feature in the Twenty20s that follow.

But despite sitting out last weekend’s warm-up match at the Waca, early fitness work on tour has seen Bethell report swelling in the same knee. Scan results have been sent back to his specialist in the UK and his tour is now officially over.

With fast bowler Josh Tongue also ruled out of the tour last week due to a toe problem, the Sussex all-rounder James Coles and Hampshire seamer Eddie Jack – both in the senior T20 squad – are flying in early from the Lions series in the Caribbean.

A bystander at training on Wednesday, Bethell will travel home this weekend and undergo further assessment on a worrying issue that has kept him out of action since the third ODI against India at Lord’s back in July.

articles.title: Littler expected 'pub players' on Netflix show
articles.summary: Luke Littler says he thought he would be facing pub players on his recent Netflix show, which was billed as giving "amateurs a chance at life-changing money".
body: Broadcast live globally on the streaming platform last month, the cash was won by top women's player Fallon Sherrock.
The format of 'Beat Luke Littler' saw 24 players selected to take on the world number one in a single leg of 501, hoping to win a prize of £501,000.
The 24-strong field did include low-level opponents, such as an Australian jockey, a bin man and a Nando's manager, but anyone who was not a member of the PDC Tour was also allowed to compete.

That meant Sherrock - who became the first female player to beat a male opponent at the PDC World Championship on her way to the last 32 in December 2019 - and leading junior players Mitchell Lawrie and Zach Griffiths were also eligible.

articles.title: Pochettino’s Manchester United interest is as natural as it is disruptive to the US
articles.summary: The former Tottenham manager is always going to be a subject of interest, but United’s job carries a rare power. As Mauricio Pochettino left the podium to close his final press conference of the last international window, he offered an ambiguous farewell.
body: “See you next …” Pochettino began as he headed to the tunnels of Allianz Field in Saint Paul, before cutting his sentence short. Then, a bit of a sing-song: “See you next, see you next.”

You don’t need an AI clanker’s autocomplete function to try closing the sentence. “See you next month” would have been synonymous with “see you next window”, after all. Still, the farewell felt poignant given questions about whether Pochettino was going to last a full four-year cycle as US men’s national team head coach.
In hindsight, maybe he had omitted adding something along the lines of: see you next, before I’m off to my next project.

From the moment that Pochettino and US Soccer announced his contract renewal in August, it was tough for many to imagine he would don his lavish safari shirts on the US sideline at the 2030 World Cup. This was Mauricio Pochettino, after all, a name brand in club management whose résumé teemed with unfinished business. Few great coaches hang their hat on being Premier League and Champions League runners-up.

articles.title: Liverpool incorrectly denied pen vs Arsenal says independent panel
articles.summary: Liverpool should have been awarded a penalty when Jurrien Timber pulled Alexander Isak's shirt in Arsenal's victory at Anfield, an independent panel has ruled.
body: The Key Match Incidents (KMI) panel assesses refereeing incidents across every Premier League match and voted 4:1 that referee Andy Madley should have awarded Liverpool a spot kick.
The panel also voted 3:2 that VAR Stuart Attwell should have intervened and sent Madley to the pitchside monitor on the basis that it was a clear and obvious error.

Arsenal led 1-0 through Kai Havertz's goal, which proved to be the winner, when Isak attempted to head Bradley Barcola's cross in the 21st minute on November 1, but was pulled back by defender Timber.

One KMI panellist believed "the short-lived holding to lack clear impact on the ability of Isak to progress", while two panellists argued, "the subjectivity in assessing impact meant this did not meet the high threshold for VAR intervention".

articles.title: Big underdogs once more, can Arsenal beat Barcelona again?
articles.summary: Arsenal face Barcelona in the Women's Champions League this week - the first time the two have met since the 2025 final when the Gunners were victorious against all odds.
body: Renee Slegers had taken charge on a permanent basis just four months before, and the showpiece finale in Lisbon - which Arsenal won 1-0 - was by far her greatest tactical victory and arguably Arsenal's most complete performance of her tenure.

"It's one of the proudest moments. That performance was immense and it had so many facets to it... We've studied Barcelona and we're in the here and now. This is a new game, a new moment," she said in her pre-match press conference.

Slegers could do with a replica on Thursday. The Gunners boss is under pressure to produce results after yet another struggling start to the season. They are already six points behind the top three in the WSL, and 12 points from league leaders Manchester City.
The Dutchwoman needs something to kickstart Arsenal's campaign - a big win to remind everyone just who this team are would help.

articles.title: From the sack in Cyprus to Liverpool: Iraola's first job explained
articles.summary: Not every successful career starts spectacularly well but Andoni Iraola's journey to Liverpool will take some beating. Seven years ago, he was sacked from his first job in management after a winless streak in the Cypriot top division with AEK Larnaca.
body: Iraola learned from the experience and rebuilt his career back in Spain with Mirandes before really impressing with Rayo Vallecano and Bournemouth to earn his opportunity at Anfield. Nevertheless, it must be curious for his old colleagues to witness the rise.

Were there any believers that day in January when Larnaca drew 2-2 at home to Ermis Aradippou, the team that would go on to finish bottom of the table? It extended the run of league games without a win to six and Iraola paid the price for that streak with his job.

Were there clues beyond the results that Iraola was destined for bigger things and merely the victim of a trigger-happy firing culture at the Cypriot club? Speaking to David Catala, who played under him at Larnaca, including in that final game, he did see promising signs.

"He already had very clear ideas of what he wanted," Catala tells Sky Sports. "You saw it and, for sure, all the players were speaking about how he was going to become a fantastic coach. But to reach this level? To say that he would be at Liverpool? That is a big claim."

articles.title: Beloved football broadcaster Danny Kelly dies aged 69
articles.summary: The popular sports broadcaster Danny Kelly has died aged 69 after a battle with cancer. A lifelong Tottenham fan, but beloved by fans from all clubs, Kelly announced earlier this year that he had been diagnosed with oesophageal cancer.
body: Kelly featured on popular shows Kick Off, Sporting Life and Trans-Euro Express, while also becoming a major part of The Athletic’s Tottenham podcast The View From The Lane as its presenter. Kelly was also a music lover and spent two years as editor of the NME.
And the football community is mourning the loss of the beloved presenter, with talkSPORT paying tribute to Kelly and sharing one of his most iconic quotes on air: “I love football, Stan. I love it.”

The broadcaster added that Kelly was “a cherished part of talkSPORT for so many years” and brought “extraordinary wit, warmth and knowledge to our airwaves. His passion for football, music and life was infectious, and his kindness touched everyone around him.”

Friend and fellow broadcaster Danny Baker said: “My great friend, supreme broadcaster and funniest man I ever knew, Danny Kelly, died yesterday afternoon. I cannot believe I will never hear his voice again.”

To get him out of that deal, United is expected to trigger Pochettino's buyout clause, which is reportedly worth around $10 million. United and U.S. Soccer have yet to make official contact, according to The Athletic's reporting.

Carrick, a former United midfielder, was named permanent manager this past offseason after impressing as interim boss following Ruben Amorim’s sacking in January. His permanent tenure lasted less than six months.
